metadata.name: QX-18-public-data-reconstruction-v0.10-strict
metadata.provenance: Real QX-18 geometry plus a fixed-revision public BR Simulator coefficient reconstruction and datasheet-based avionics profiles

assumptions: The BR Simulator data are engineering-model values, not QX-18 flight-test identified coefficients
Unity principal inertia and rotation are transformed to the documented FRD tensor convention
The BR longitudinal formula is sampled without ground effect; the table is deliberately limited to -5 through 8 degrees and does not model stall
A one-to-one KRS-4034HV linkage is assumed for both rudder and elevator; actual QX-18 actuator dynamics are not public
Servo time constant, deadband and command resolution are explicit engineering assumptions because the manufacturer does not specify them
Nominal sensor biases are zero; datasheet accuracy limits belong in later Monte Carlo uncertainty cases
Pitot coefficient is one and tubing dynamics beyond the SDP810 response are not identified
The 100 Hz differential-pressure and angle clocks represent the production firmware polling rate; SDP810 internal updates are faster and AS5600 default-filter step response is about 2.2 ms
Ground-climb feedback updates only for distinct 32 Hz barometric samples; its -0.25 m/s barrier is a deterministic stress setting rather than a flight-identified requirement
Invalid-airspeed altitude-loss blending is referenced to the simulated release altitude and is not flight-identified
The strict scenario starts at the analytic 9.698 m/s steady glide and terminates if angle of attack leaves the -5 through 8 degree table
The reference-controller schedule is a software test strategy, not a flight-test-identified QX-18 controller
Ground-climb feedback differentiates a noise-free sample-and-hold barometric altitude and applies a 0.15 second filter; transport delay, weather pressure changes and sensor faults are not modeled
Ground effect corrects only the induced-drag term; BR downwash, tail-lift and pitching-moment ground effects are not reconstructed

reference_geometry.moment_reference: BR Simulator centre of mass transformed to body x forward, y right, z down
